details.description: MiniMax-M2 is a text-only Mixture-of-Experts language model from MiniMax, released October 27, 2025, built for coding and long-horizon agentic tool-use workflows. It has 230 billion total parameters with only 10 billion activated per token, an architecture aimed at fast, cost-efficient inference while running shell, browser, retrieval, and code-execution tool chains. It supports function calling and multi-step tool orchestration. MiniMax has since released newer text models (M2.1, M2.5, M2.7, and M3) that supersede it in its own lineup.
advantages: Scores 69.4% on SWE-bench Verified, per MiniMax's model card.
Scores 83 on LiveCodeBench and 82 on MMLU-Pro, per MiniMax's model card.
Ranked #1 among open-weight models on Artificial Analysis's composite intelligence benchmark at launch, per MiniMax's model card.
MiniMax reports the model generates at roughly 100 tokens per second, nearly double the speed it attributes to comparable larger models, in its launch announcement.
disadvantages: Text-only model that does not accept image or other non-text input, per MiniMax's model card and Fireworks AI's model listing.
MiniMax has since released newer text models (M2.1, M2.5, M2.7, and M3); M2 is no longer featured among MiniMax's current models on its site.
use_cases: Coding tasks such as multi-file edits, run-fix loops, and test-validated repairs
Agentic tool use across shell, browser, retrieval, and code-execution tools
Long-horizon agent workflows that require stable, multi-step tool calling

notes: Catalog facts list max_input_tokens up to 1,000,000 and max_output_tokens up to 8,000 across this model's providers, while MiniMax's and Fireworks' own pages describe a roughly 196K-token context window instead; kept the catalog's values as authoritative and did not restate a specific context figure. Release-date and supersession claims rely on minimax.io and GitHub pages that were paraphrased by an automated page-summarization step; the core benchmark numbers were corroborated across three independently fetched pages (Hugging Face rendered page, Hugging Face raw README, GitHub README).
